title: Photo 054 · 아워글래스 USSBBW · 은입사 · 무릎 꿇기 정면 (한쪽 무릎) · 동아프리카 30대 후반
prompt:
Image format: a vertical portrait-orientation photograph, 2:3 aspect ratio, taller than it is wide.

A full-body photograph on a plain seamless mid-grey backdrop, nothing in the frame but a low flat platform, shot on a medium format camera with an 85mm lens at f/8, a single hard key light raking in from one side so the texture of the skin stands out, sharp focus from head to toe, realistic photographic grain — a real photograph, not an illustration, not CGI, not a render.

Subject: ONE real adult East African woman in her late 30s, deep umber skin tone with a warm sheen, her face exactly the same tone as her body, real skin texture with visible pores and fine grain, two thick braided buns, a calm confident expression, real living eyes. She wears double-hoop earrings and has sharp talon-shaped nails.

Physique: An extraordinarily large woman, far beyond any real person, her body so wide that her hips are cut off by the left and right edges of the frame. A colossal heavy bust far wider than her shoulders, and below it a waistline that still draws in clearly even at this size — a shadowed groove running around her middle, the one place on her body where the outline pulls inward. Below that waistline an immense mass of soft heavy fat sits on her middle and drops straight down from it under its own weight, projecting far forward past the line of her own knees before it falls, settling onto the tops of her thighs and piling over them, gathering into three or four heavy rounded folds as it falls, deep shadowed creases between them, the surface soft and uneven, never taut, never smooth, never round like a drum. It merges seamlessly into her sides, her hips and her thighs with no boundary anywhere, one continuous body rather than a separate mass, not pregnant. Colossal hips more than three times the width of that waistline and a gigantic rounded rear, each thigh thicker than a normal woman's waist, thick heavy calves, very thick upper arms, a full round face. Her head looks small on top of her massive body and her hands look small against her thighs. Wide at the bust, drawn in at the waistline, wide again below: the silhouette reads as a great hourglass at the most extreme size. Every fold and curve keeps its own clear rounded outline with a deep shadowed crease between them, never merging into one shapeless mass. Her arms, hands, legs and feet stay in correct proportion to each other. The sheer weight of the flesh is visible in how it drops, settles and presses down onto the thighs beneath it.

Skin: Real photographic skin — visible pores and fine grain, natural creases and shadow where the flesh folds, faint stretch marks where the great curves have expanded, the raking light picking out every ridge and hollow of the surface. No smooth illustration finish, no plastic CG sheen.

Body Art: Her bare skin is painted in Korean eunipsa silver inlay style — a deep black ground with thick bright silver linework covering most of the surface, fine lattice fills between the lines, a bold silver band following every deep crease and curving around the hips and thighs like contour lines. The paint is pigment sitting on living skin, so it distorts slightly over every bulge and cracks a little where the skin folds. The paint covers her whole body with no bare skin left anywhere below the jaw: her shoulders, her upper arms, her forearms and the backs of her hands are painted as densely as her torso, and so are the sides of her body, her back, her rear, the lower belly, the knees, the calves and the tops of her feet. Her face is left unpainted and the pattern fades out at the neck with no hard line.

Pose: Kneeling on one knee on the platform facing the camera, one shin and foot folded back beneath her with that thigh lying flat, the other knee raised in front of her with the foot planted flat on the platform, the great mass of her middle settling down over the flat thigh on one side and pressing against the raised thigh on the other, her back straight, her hands resting on her thighs with her arms held clear of her body so nothing crosses in front of her torso, her head level and facing the lens, full body head to feet filling the frame.

Footwear: Extreme silver platform stiletto mules with a squared toe band, the platform soles as tall as her ankle bones, the ultra-thin stiletto heels so high her insteps stand nearly vertical.

Background & Lighting: the silver linework catching the light unevenly the way paint on skin does rather than like real metal, the hard raking light carving every fold and curve.

Vertical 2:3 portrait-orientation full-body photograph, taller than it is wide.
